Kit

kit/xfer — chunked large payloads

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
How it routesSending and receivingRetain payloads for late joiners with Album

Use a transfer to send a large payload, such as a user-drawn spray, custom skin, or shared level file. kit/xfer splits it into chunks, limits the number sent per tick, and reassembles it at each receiver. This bounds transfer work per tick and avoids submitting the entire payload as one transport message. For WebRTC without SCTP message interleaving, RFC 8831 recommends limiting messages to 16KB to avoid monopolizing the association; this is not a universal WebRTC message-size cap.

An entity blob sends its complete contents on each version change and is included in snapshots for joiners. A transfer sends a payload once. Use the Album described below when late joiners also need that payload.

Transfers use the session's app channel independently of either simulation model. Consume arrivals in frame code, then use events or fields to represent their consequences. Do not consume them inside a simulation tick: network arrival timing is not deterministic simulation input.

How it routes#

All transfers route through the host. A client sends paced 8KB frames; the host assembles its own copy and relays each frame with the sender identity. Other peers accept these broadcasts only from the host. The sender already holds the original bytes and does not receive a completion event for its own transfer.

ksess.Host_Relay handles sender identity, source checks, echo policy, and delivery to individual peers. Xfer adds chunk encoding, assembly, and replacement of superseded payloads. It sets echo = false, suppressing returned copies of client uploads and local delivery of the host's own broadcasts.

Sending and receiving#

Odin
import kxfer "godot:kit/xfer"

kxfer.xfer_init(&self.xfer, &self.ses, MY_TAG) // once; choose a unique tag: the
                                               // default (2) collides if the
                                               // game already claimed it
kxfer.xfer_send(&self.xfer, PAYLOAD_ID, bytes) // anyone; ≤512KB; copies
kxfer.xfer_pump(&self.xfer)                    // once per net tick; sends at most
                                               // 2 x 8KB chunks/tick
                                               // ≈ 320KB/s at the default 20Hz;
                                               // the cap scales with tick_hz, and
                                               // transfer work per tick is bounded.
for {                                          // every frame
    ev, ok := kxfer.xfer_poll(&self.xfer)
    if !ok { break }
    #partial switch e in ev {
    case kxfer.Ev_Done: // e.from, e.id, e.bytes — decode/copy this frame
    }
}

Payloads are keyed by (sender, id byte). Sending the same ID again replaces the queued copy and restarts assembly at receivers. Because the reliable channel preserves per-sender order, sequence gaps indicate a restart rather than packet loss. Receivers discard an assembly if its total exceeds MAX_PAYLOAD (512KB) or its chunk count is inconsistent. Senders do not receive their own Ev_Done; the album can retain a local copy and report it through the same polling API as received payloads.

Worked example. In scrapyard's spray-wall integration test, act 12 reads a PNG from user://spray.png and transfers it to peers at startup. Pressing G then places the spray on the floor. Placement uses a 13-byte kcomms marker because peers already hold the image. The test injects 120ms latency and requires the byte counts printed on both sides to match exactly.

Retain payloads for late joiners with Album#

A raw transfer is not retained for later joiners. Album caches payloads by player and kind, stores local submissions immediately, and reports arrivals for the game to decode and display. The host can replay its cached payloads to late joiners through the same paced transfer mechanism:

Odin
kxfer.album_init(&self.album, &self.ses, MY_TAG)  // instead of xfer_init
kxfer.album_put(&self.album, SPRAY_ID, png)       // cache locally now; send through album_pump
kxfer.album_pump(&self.album)                     // once per net tick
for {                                             // poll each frame for changed payloads
	from, id, ok := kxfer.album_poll(&self.album)
	if !ok {break}
	bytes, _ := kxfer.album_get(&self.album, from, id) // owned by the album; decode, don't retain
}

// Host, on Ev_Player_Joined, including rejoins that may have lost their cache:
// replay retained payloads to this player using the live-send chunk budget.
kxfer.album_welcome(&self.album, e.id)

Putting the same key again replaces the payload and cancels in-flight catch-up of the older copy, preventing two chunk streams from competing for one assembly. Album stores bytes; the game owns decoded images or other artifacts and uses album_poll to decide when to decode again. Headless tests in tests/kitxfer cover chunked convergence, replacement, and addressed catch-up.
